paragraphs: The Z4 sDrive35i uses the N54 engine — a 3.0-litre twin-turbocharged inline-six petrol, fitted throughout the E89 generation's production run from 2009 to 2016. The N54 was BMW's first production turbocharged petrol engine since the 2002 Turbo, and it represented a significant shift in the brand's engine strategy at the time, replacing the naturally aspirated N52 in the performance-oriented Z4 models. The sDrive35i sat above the sDrive30i in the Z4 range, offering considerably more power and a very different driving character — the twin-turbo setup delivers strong mid-range torque that the naturally aspirated six couldn't match. The N54 is also shared with the 135i, 335i, and 535i of the same era, which means parts availability and specialist knowledge are well-established, even though the engine itself has a distinct set of known wear points.
about.boldParagraph: The Z4 sDrive35i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

compatibility.intro: The Z4 sDrive35i uses a single engine across its entire production run — the N54 — so compatibility is relatively straightforward compared to variants that span multiple engine codes. However, there are still important details to confirm before any work starts: production-year differences in the HPFP and injector revisions, whether your car has the manual or DCT transmission (which affects certain ancillary fitments), and the ECU software version your car is running — all of which influence the parts we order and the way we approach the rebuild. This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Z4 sDrive35i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
